extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on applying AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 prior art rules and statutory exceptions (grace period, inventor-originated disclosures, U.S. patent document prior art under 102(a)(2), effective filing dates, and related affidavit/declaration practice) for examination and applicant responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace Period Inventor Disclosure Exception (AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure that would otherwise qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) will not be treated as prior art if: (1) the disclosure was made one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; and (2) the disclosure is by the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel determine necessary evidence case-by-case depending on whether it is apparent from the disclosure itself or the patent application specification that the disclosure is by the inventor or a joint inventor. If the disclosure (e.g., publication) names the inventor/joint inventor as author/inventor and does not name additional authors/joint inventors and is within one year, it will be treated as a grace period inventor disclosure and not prior art. If the publication names additional persons not named in the application, it may be treated as prior art. Applicants may include a statement designating grace period inventor disclosures in the specification (see 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6) and MPEP § 608.01(a)) and may provide a copy of the disclosure to expedite examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/Declaration to Establish Inventor Disclosure Exception (37 CFR 1.130 / MPEP §2155.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: When it is not apparent from the prior disclosure or the patent application specification that the prior disclosure is by the inventor or a joint inventor, the applicant may establish by affidavit or declaration that a grace period disclosure was by the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 (see MPEP §2155.01) to show that a prior disclosure is not prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) because it was by the inventor or a joint inventor. The sufficiency and type of evidence are handled case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace Period Inventor-Originated Disclosure Exception (AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure otherwise qualifying as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) may be excepted if: (1) it was made one year or less before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; and (2) it was made by another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may establish via affidavit/declaration that the intervening disclosure was by someone who obtained the subject matter from the inventor or joint inventor (see MPEP §718 and §2155.03). Evidence requirements handled case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening Disclosure Exception Focusing on Subject Matter (AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure that would otherwise be prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) may be excepted if the subject matter disclosed in the intervening disclosure had, before such disclosure, been publicly disclosed by the inventor, a joint inventor, or another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception focuses on the subject matter, not the mode of disclosure; the prior disclosure need not be in the same form or verbatim. The exception may apply only to portions of the intervening disclosure that were previously publicly disclosed (e.g., if prior disclosure included elements A,B,C and intervening shows A,B,C,D, then only D is prior art). Examples: species/genus rules (a prior-disclosed species can render a later-disclosed genus excepted for the genus; converse yields prior art for the species). Determination under 102(b)(1)(B) does not compare subject matter to the claimed invention — that is handled under anticipation/obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) — U.S. Patent Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) makes certain U.S. patent documents prior art as of the date they were effectively filed with respect to the subject matter relied upon if they name another inventor: (1) U.S. patents; (2) U.S. patent application publications; and (3) certain WIPO published applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'U.S. patent documents' may have different prior art effects under pre-AIA §102(e) than under AIA §102(a)(2). A document may also be prior art under 102(a)(1) if its issue/publication date is before the effective filing date. See MPEP §§2151, 2154, and 2154.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO PCT Publications as U.S. Patent Application Publications for 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO publications of PCT international applications that designate the United States are treated as U.S. patent application publications for prior art purposes under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), regardless of international filing date, English language, or whether the PCT enters the U.S. national stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This AIA treatment differs from pre-AIA 102(e) treatment which had additional requirements (e.g., filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, designated US, published in English). See MPEP §2136.03 for pre-AIA discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining 'Effectively Filed' Date Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 102(a)(2) purposes, a U.S. patent document is prior art as of either its actual filing date or the filing date of a prior application to which it claims priority/benefit (per 35 U.S.C. 102(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A U.S. patent document is 'entitled to claim' priority/benefit if it contains the priority/benefit claim, was filed within applicable filing period, and has a common inventor or same applicant. The 102(d) 'effectively filed' concept differs from entitlement to priority under other statutes; examiners need not evaluate whether any claim is actually entitled to priority under §§119/120/121/365/386 when applying a document as prior art under 102(d). See MPEP §2152.01 and MPEP §2136.03 for related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: AIA Eliminates Hilmer Doctrine for 102(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d), a U.S. patent document that claims priority to prior-filed foreign or international applications is effectively filed as of the earliest such application that describes the subject matter, eliminating the pre-AIA Hilmer doctrine limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus foreign priority dates may be used for a U.S. patent document's effective prior art date under AIA 102(d) if the earlier application describes the subject matter; for applications where AIA changes do not apply, Hilmer may still control. See MPEP §2136 for nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement That the U.S. Patent Document 'Names Another Inventor' (102(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2), the U.S. patent document must 'name another inventor' — i.e., the inventive entity of the prior document must differ from that of the application under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any difference in inventive entity suffices; in joint inventorship contexts only one joint inventor needs to be different. Even with common inventors, the document qualifies as prior art under 102(a)(2) unless an applicable 102(b)(2) exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) for Copending U.S. Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an earlier filed, copending, unpublished U.S. patent application discloses subject matter that would anticipate claims in a later-filed application with a different inventive entity, the examiner should determine whether a provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional rejection is appropriate when an earlier-filed copending application, if published or patented, would be prior art under 102. Such provisional rejections can be overcome in the same manner as 102(a)(2) rejections (see MPEP §2152.06) or by abandoning and refiling a new application containing subject matter of both. Use form paragraph 7.15.01.aia for provisional 102(a)(2) rejections. If copending applications have at least one common inventor/applicant or are commonly assigned and effective filing dates differ, provisional rejection should be made. If there is no common inventor/applicant/assignee and the earlier application is unpublished under 35 U.S.C. 122(a), confidentiality must be maintained and no rejection relying on the unpublished application can be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Exception Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(A) (Inventor-Originated Disclosure) for 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure that would otherwise be prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) may be excepted if the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor (102(b)(2)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may use affidavits/declarations (see MPEP §2155.03) to show the disclosure was by another who obtained the subject matter from the inventor or joint inventor. This exception parallels the inventor-originated exception for 102(a)(1) but applies to U.S. patent documents under 102(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Exception Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(B) (Inventor or Inventor-Originated Prior Public Disclosure) for 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure that would otherwise be prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) may be excepted if the subject matter disclosed had been previously publicly disclosed by the inventor, a joint inventor, or another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from them (102(b)(2)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with 102(b)(1)(B), the exception focuses on subject matter and not mode or verbatim identity of disclosure. The exception may apply only to previously disclosed subject matter (partial exception); genus/species examples apply similarly. Affidavits/declarations may be used to show prior public disclosure by the inventor or originator (see MPEP §§2155.02, 2155.03). Determination under 102(b)(2)(B) does not involve comparison to the claimed invention (anticipation/obviousness is separate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Exception Under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) (Common Ownership or Obligation of Assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art exception exists under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) based on common ownership or obligation of assignment that can prevent a U.S. patent document from being used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section header present in the guidance (MPEP §2154.02(c)). The chunked text ends before detailed explanation; see MPEP §2154.02(c) for procedures, required evidence, and how common ownership/obligation of assignment is applied to except a U.S. patent document from prior art effect.
